title: Access intake signal fusion and policy-driven routing
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Enterprise customers are sending a high volume of admin & access requests (RBAC role templates, SSO/SAML onboarding, SCIM provisioning, org policy exceptions). The current intake funnel is one-size-fits-all which creates noise for SRE/Platform teams and slows SLA for high-risk requests. We need a deterministic, auditable triage layer that fuses signals (request metadata, requester role, customer contract tier, recent incidents, and explicit policy flags) into a priority score and routes requests to the appropriate path: automated action, delegated operator review, or enterprise escalation.
scope: Design and implement a scoring + routing pipeline for admin/access intake. Includes updated intake form schema, signal extractor, scoring heuristics, routing rules, basic UI changes in Console intake view, and playbooks for operator review. Integrations: SSO/SAML metadata validator, SCIM capability checker, RBAC sensitivity classifier, and links to customer contract/SLAs in CRM.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Intake form collects normalized attributes for RBAC, SSO, SCIM, and org-policy requests and validates required fields.
2) Signal fusion engine produces a reproducible priority score (0-100) and primary routing decision for each request.
3) Rules for automated handling (low-risk) vs operator queue (medium) vs enterprise SLA path (high) are configurable and stored in Console.
4) Every routed request records the signals used and the scoring breakdown in audit logs accessible from the Console request detail.
5) Security review checklist completed and KMS keys used where required for sensitive attachments.
6) End-to-end tests and a small canary roll out run with 3 pilot customers showing mean time to resolution improvement >= 40% for high-priority enterprise requests.

2026-03-04 - PM decision: Use hybrid rules+ML heuristics. Phase 1 = rules-driven weighted scoring; Phase 2 = replace weights with learned model based on labeled historical requests. Trade-off noted: ML adds calibration time and dataset curation overhead. (Maya)

2026-03-06 - Security review: Need explicit consent and redaction guidance for attachments; ensure SAML metadata not stored in plaintext logs. Security checklist at: https://drive.redwood/security/admin-intake-checklist.pdf (SEC)
2026-03-08 - Ops: Proposed operator queues split by domain (RBAC ops, SSO onboarding, SCIM provisioning). Also propose 'fast-track' for accounts on Dedicated/Dedicated+SLA. (Ops)

2026-03-10 - Sync: Finalized scoring buckets and initial weights. Agreed roll out plan: pilot with three enterprise customers, monitor false positives/negatives, iterate. Added ENG task to add audit log schema. (All)
